_readme: STABLE COLD FAILURES — the roster of golden-set cases that are HARD assertions (NOT knownIssue, NOT excused by anything) and that fail on EVERY COLD run of run-eval.ts (`--nocache`, which also sends nosave=1 and debug=1). The set is measured as the exact INTERSECTION over three restarted cold runs on one build, never from a single run's total — that is what makes a documented rotator distinguishable from a new member. This file exists so that 'is this a NEW cold failure?' is a diff instead of a reading exercise: the set previously lived only in prose across three documents, they disagreed about its size, and a ten quietly became a nine with nothing in the repo noticing. Check a cold run against it with: npm run eval:cold-set. Members here are STANDING DEBT, not absolution — every one still reds a cold run, exactly as it should.
_notTheSameAs: known-issue-baseline.json / known-issue-baseline-cold.json are the OPPOSITE population and answer a different question. Those pin the per-case OBSERVED VALUES (foodId, foodName, grams, kcal100, abstained, errored, itemCount) of cases flagged `knownIssue` in golden-set.json — cases that are already EXCUSED, whose failure run-eval deliberately does not count (evalExitCode ignores them), and whose only remaining signal is DRIFT: 'still failing, but failing DIFFERENTLY', reported explicitly NON-GATING at run-eval.ts:427. This file pins MEMBERSHIP, not values, for cases that are NOT excused: they are real red and they fail the suite. The two sets are provably disjoint — no id below appears among the 21 knownIssue ids in golden-set.json, nor among the 20 ids pinned in known-issue-baseline.json (verified 2026-08-19). A knownIssue case can therefore never be a member here, and the checker enforces that.
_naming: The nightly WARM sweep prints a bare count for its own, different set: `known issues still failing: N` (10 of 21 on 2026-08-19, with 11 now passing). This set's size is also nine-or-ten-ish, is measured on a different instrument (COLD, not warm), over a different population (HARD, not excused), and means the opposite thing. Two bare numbers of similar magnitude on one page is exactly how the ten-that-became-a-nine survived. So this set is never 'the failures' and never a bare N: it is `stable cold failures`, and check-stable-cold-failures.ts stamps that label on every line it prints.
_notAnAllowlist: This file is a DETECTOR for the cold session gate, never an excuse list. It is not read by flywheel-sweep.ts, it is not wired to --allow-fail (which defaults EMPTY by design and is pinned by the doc-check claim `flywheel-allow-fail-defaults-empty`), and it cannot turn a red nightly green. The nightly goes green when real failures get FIXED. Membership here is the standing bill; the way a member leaves is check-stable-cold-failures.ts reporting LEFT THE SET after someone fixed it, confirmed over 2-3 cold runs, and then removed it from this file.
_rotatorsNote: THREE mechanisms flap this set, not one. (1) AI serving-gram draws on a fixed record (count_unit_ai / AiGeneratedServing, and fdc_size_estimate) -- n-brand-02, n-serv-26, n-svd-03, n-svd-04 (added 2026-09-09; the test that settled it was the WITHIN-BUILD pass/fail split, 12 of 13 NAMED failing builds also carrying a pass, not the fixed winner), and n-prose-10 (added 2026-09-15 on the same test: 7 of its 8 named failing builds also carry a pass). (2) A RETRIEVAL TIE that re-rolls on the Typesense-state axis, never on a recipe-api restart -- n-prot-04, added 2026-09-04; and n-svg-03, added 2026-09-15 on the census shape _membershipMethodBlindSpot prescribes (seven cold winners, only two of which ever failed), NOT on co-movement: its winner changes fell between consecutive cold runs that moved 19 to 157 nlp winners at once, so moving alongside n-prot-04 carries little information. A full rebuild is the documented trigger; what moved winners in the 2026-09-12/09-15 gap, which holds no recorded rebuild, is UNVERIFIED. (3) An LLM SEGMENTER item-count draw on a composite line -- n-prose-13, added 2026-09-06: the assertion there is expectItems, so what flaps is HOW MANY items came back, not which record won or what it weighed; a rotator of this shape is invisible to every foodId/grams diff you would normally reach for. If a NEW rotator is proposed, check whether it is one of these mechanisms before adding it here rather than fixing it.

causeLegend.PANEL: the winning record's own nutrition panel is wrong (usually an uncaught corrupt OFF row, corruptReason NULL)
causeLegend.SERVING: the right record is picked but the wrong serving rung bills it
causeLegend.PICK: retrieval or ranking selects the wrong record
causeLegend.IDENTITY: the record is a brandless stub carrying a different food's values — repairing its panel would still miss the band

members.reason: off_9348470000900 'Unsweetened Almond Milk' carries kcal100=60 against a [10, 45] band (real ~13-17). Its panel is Atwater-coherent but physically impossible (fiber 4.8 g vs fat 3.5 g per 100 ml), so the calories were computed from wrong macros; corruptReason is NULL, so no detector reaches it. Explicitly NOT a modifier-drop case — the query already resolves to a record NAMED 'Unsweetened Almond Milk'.

Bare 'apple' cold-resolves to off_9333022029263 at kcal100=23.9 against a [35, 75] band (real ~52). The panel is Atwater-INcoherent on its own macros, corruptReason is NULL, and the 1-token name puts it squarely in the ~61% detector-unreachable population. Warm is green only because the key was repointed to FDC 171688 as a human-triage pin on 2026-08-03; cold retrieval has never selected that record unaided.

Bare 'mayonnaise' bills fs_34194 at 14.7 g — grams INSIDE the intended band — but the record is a LIGHT-mayo panel (390 kcal/100g) sitting under the bare generic name, so total.calories=57.0 falls under the [60, 180] band. Warm is masked by a human-triage FoodMapping row; the failure is the panel, not the rung.

Bare 'bacon' bills 5 g against a [10, 40] band. That 5 g is FatSecret's own default label on fs_1517, '1 thin slice (yield after cooking)'; in-band 8/12/28 g labels exist on the SAME record and are never picked, because fs_default_serving is deliberately not in the serving guard's REPLACE_TIERS. The PR D pt3 cured/breakfast-meat lexicon default (~28 g) therefore never fires here.

Bare 'pepper jack' bills 2.5 g against an [18, 40] band. The winner off_0858815007307's ONLY serving label is the degenerate '100 g (100 g)' placeholder, which is billed and then CAPPED 100 -> 2.5 g by the spice lexicon matching the contained 'pepper' token: label_serving_default sits in plain CAP_TIERS, while the head-gate fix protects only bare_label_serving. NOTE: the golden-set note's premise of a 'genuine 28 g slice label' is FALSE for this particular winner.

The documented #18 brand-bearing chain regression: 'noodles and company pad thai' bills a brandless retail dry-noodle record (off_4099100064773, 127.5 g via bare_name_sibling_serving) instead of fs_81276 [Noodles & Company]. fs_81276 now carries NULL per-100g calories and a gramless serving, which plausibly handicaps it at admission/scoring. The 2026-07-25 warm recovery was a pure cache eviction, not a retrieval fix, which is exactly why the case is still red cold.

DELIBERATE RED per its golden-set note. PR #235 (2026-08-04) added a total.calories band precisely so the ~30% over-bill would stop being invisible: cold maps '1 cup cooked black beans' to a saucy OFF composite (off_0039400019442) at 240 g / 295 kcal against the USDA reference 172 g / 227 kcal. '12 m&ms' bills grams=264 against a [6, 25] band on fs_72448178 "M&M'S" [Cold Stone Creamery] — a mix-in record whose serving rows carry no grams, discarded as no_nutrition until K3 (#390, deployed 2026-08-26) stopped rejecting gram-less FS rows. Conditional on that win the billed grams are a DRAW: 264 on four observed draws, 22 on a fifth (22 g / 110 kcal would PASS the band), tier fs_default_serving — so the 264 is the record's own serving row, not K3's synthetic kcal/2 grams. The resurrection is K3's; the draw is not. COLD-ONLY and unreachable by live traffic: the warm cache row is keyed 'm ms' -> off_00005579 (usedCount 363, untouched) while the cold pipeline keys "m m's", the documented apostrophe/plural fork. The K3 gate could not have seen it — a record that stops returning null is a POOL change, and its 48-seed cross-snapshot arm was venue lines plus controls. The real fix is the resurrected-record pick class (same-name cross-source picks where K3 newly admits a gram-less FS record), A8 pick-family work rather than a per-seed hack; this entry documents the debt and excuses nothing.

rotators.mechanism: segmenter draw on a composite line
rotators.reason: The assertion is expectItems >= 7 on a seven-food prose line, and the failing draw reads `expected >=7 items, got 3` (7 of the 9 real sightings) or `got 2` (2 of them): the whole `... scrambled with a bit of chopped bell peppers, onions, mushrooms, and spinach ...` clause comes back as ONE composite item, observed.foodName 'Scrambled Egg Whites with Bell Peppers, Onions, Mushrooms...' on an ai_estimated cuid (cmsyc7s4r008kw3wwcaerhe7b x4, cmszacjk9008jxw81gc0khrpl, cmtate9le008ksb1chaz2spqt) or 'whole cooked scrambled egg' fdc_172187 x3. So this is an ITEM-COUNT draw: not a grams draw, not a retrieval tie, and it says nothing about which record won. WHICH LAYER produces the composite -- the seg-v2 segmenter drawing a `dish` reading, or the mapper merging split items -- is NOT instrumented; `mechanism` above names the observable, not a located cause (the golden-set note flags the segmenter reading as HYPOTHESIS, NOT MEASURED, and it still is). CENSUS over the 535 eval-*.json files in scripts/eval/results/ (2026-09-06; all 535 parse, 89 of them executed this case): 12 failing rows, of which 3 are HTTP 401 TRANSPORT rows from 2026-08-21 (the documented DEV_API_KEY-not-in-shell-env trap) and are not failures of this case, leaving 9 real sightings across 8 distinct build ids -- B4HEbh1SKj7NmLZEFdWh_, 1cGQ1yKWfIC0Th7GXIJf4, 6X4EdJlSKyX9V-6MWf4ZU, JVSJtRRqnjbw23d9sIIjF x2, WJMIDfm60hb3sMF4gjG35, modTvpChRBqrlz0w3x-qw, Qw2-DAKAAv_KmvvDzrUo3, bpN24cIkZNxBLOFMoss3G. Raw real-failure rate 9 of 89 = 10.1%. READ THE DENOMINATOR: one of those nine (6X4EdJlSKyX9V-6MWf4ZU, 2026-08-18T23:20Z) was recorded while the case still carried knownIssue:true, and a knownIssue row is not a HARD failure for this instrument at all -- the case was pinned by 4ef8b96 on 2026-08-18 and promoted back to HARD by b7f8a9b on 2026-08-20 (`pins := flags`), which is why 11 of the 89 appearances are excused-at-run-time. Restricted to the population this detector actually judges, COLD and HARD, it is 8 of 60 = 13.3% across 7 build ids. Both framings are ~1 run in 8-10; quote either WITH its denominator, never the bare count. It also flapped on the UNCHANGED BASE TREE of that same session 40 A/B on 2026-09-05 -- base IM7gvTj9lTHINLfw3oVXG red on run 3 of 3 with runs 1-2 green, while the branch arm JAST9NialoAx3O_R5e4Oq passed 3/3 -- so it is NOT attributable to any PR under gate, the same base-tree control `confirmedAgainst` applies to the other rotators. WHY A ROTATOR AND NOT A MEMBER: 8 HARD sightings spread over 7 build ids at ~10% is the signature of a per-request draw, which is exactly what the three-restarted-run intersection test is built to exclude, and adding it to `members` would make check-stable-cold-failures.ts print LEFT THE SET on the next clean run and invite someone to attribute a fix that never happened -- the same reasoning the file already applies to n-prot-04, reached by the opposite route: n-prot-04 is INVISIBLE to the intersection test (see _membershipMethodBlindSpot) whereas this one is visible to it and correctly excluded by it. _membershipMethodBlindSpot: THE MEMBERSHIP TEST IS BLIND TO MECHANISM (2). Membership is measured as the exact INTERSECTION over three RESTARTED cold runs on ONE build. That distinguishes a per-request draw (mechanism 1) from a stable failure, because a draw re-rolls between restarts. It CANNOT distinguish a retrieval tie that re-rolls only on a Typesense rebuild (mechanism 2): within one build such a tie is parked on one side, so three restarted runs agree 3/3 and the case looks exactly like a stable member. n-prot-04 was proposed as member #10 twice on that evidence -- 2026-08-11 (§10u, correctly adjudicated a rotator) and 2026-09-04 (Lane A S37, 3/3 on the live build). The test that settles mechanism 2 is a CROSS-BUILD census of scripts/eval/results/eval-*.json, not more runs on one build. Re-derive for any candidate: count the runs where the case failed, and group them by observed.foodId -- a tie shows several winners of which only some fail.
